quotes.text: You think you're choosing hosting, but you're actually choosing a feature set because the plan carries the domain name, the staging slot, and the ability to scale.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the hosting decision as a feature decision made by the plan.

quotes.text: A virtual machine is a computer you rent, and everything on it is your problem, from the operating system upward. App service is a service you rent, and the operating system is never your problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp contrast between IaaS and PaaS responsibility.

quotes.text: Compute is dedicated at the plan level, not the app level, and that sentence deserves a second reading. If you want one app to have its own resources, the answer is a second plan rather than a setting.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the most common App Service capacity misunderstanding.

quotes.text: A swap moves more than your code, app settings and connection strings travel with the swap unless you mark them as slot settings, which is how a team ends up with a production app talking to a test database.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete warning about a frequent and costly slot-swap mistake.

quotes.text: So a rule that adds five instances at lunchtime shows up on the bill at the end of the month. Scaling is a dial with a price attached, not a free switch.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable reminder that scaling out has a direct cost.

chapters.title: What Azure App Service actually is
Mistakes beginners make and the short version

takeaways: In Azure App Service you buy an App Service plan, and its tier decides which features such as custom domains, deployment slots, Always On and autoscale you can switch on.
All apps in one plan share the same machines and scale together, so production and test environments belong in separate plans.
Deployment slots allow warm, reversible swaps into production, but app settings and connection strings move with the swap unless they are pinned as slot settings.
hook: Beginners often pick an Azure App Service tier as if it were just a size, then discover it gates domains, slots and scaling. This plain-English guide for developers and Power Platform makers explains plans, tiers, deployment slots and scaling so you can start on the right tier and avoid costly mistakes.
